question.prompt: When \(10^{93} - 93\) is expressed as a single whole number, the sum of the digits is

solutions.explanation:
Subtracting \(1\) first makes the long subtraction easier. The number \(10^{93}\) is \(1\) followed by \(93\) zeros, so \(10^{93}-1\) consists of \(93\) nines.

To subtract \(93\) in all, we must now subtract another \(92\):
\[
10^{93}-93=(10^{93}-1)-92.
\]
The last two digits change from \(99\) to \(07\), since \(99-92=7\). This requires no borrowing from the earlier digits, so the first \(91\) digits remain nines. Hence the digit sum is
\[
91\times9+0+7=826.
\]
The answer is \(826\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
